newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares on way up again after correction.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares on way up again after correction.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Wednesday after two days of correction in a quiet market with players holding back ahead of the upcoming corporate results season but with more gains seen as distinctly possible.

"The market recovered today but turnover was thin with investors awaiting the 1996 company results, which start pouring in next week. If the Dow finishes up, we'll see advances here tomorrow," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 1.39 point to 152.86, while the KFX March future rose 1.30 point to 152.15 with 260 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

NKT was much in the focus, closing 35 crowns higher at 388 after announcing a major North Sea cable order. Sophus Berendsen steamed on to end 31 crowns up at 920 and ISS put on four crowns to finish at 178.
B&O was in the limelight too, rising 10 crowns to 335 and Novo Nordisk, benefitting from the stronger dollar, closed eight up at 598.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.2 billion crowns.
